chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Isma'il ibn Jabr said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who confessed to one of his heirs a debt upon himself while he was ill. He said: It is valid for him if he confesses to it for less than one-third.

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a debt or right
key_terms.مَرِيضُ الْمَمَاتِ: A person who is ill and near death (dying person)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a dying person admits to owing a debt to one of their heirs?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a dying person's acknowledgment of a debt to a specific heir is legally valid as long as it does not exceed one-third of the total estate, preventing the depletion of the remaining inheritance. This ruling safeguards the rights of other heirs by limiting the portion of the estate that can be allocated to settle debts or bequests during the final illness (marad al-mawt).
